logline: A demon named Justitia is banished from hell and inhabits the body of a human judge, tasked with condemning ten remorseless killers on Earth - until a sharp-eyed detective starts noticing the pattern.

bollymeter.basis: IMDb audience rates it 7.8/10; it averaged 10.8% nationwide ratings on SBS and placed sixth on TIME Magazine's 10 Best K-Dramas of 2024 list. The open-ended finale and early pacing issues temper an otherwise entertaining supernatural procedural.

seasons.review_body: The Judge from Hell premiered on SBS in September 2024 and landed as one of the year's most-discussed fantasy-crime hybrids. Park Shin-hye plays double duty as the human Judge Kang Bit-na and the demon Justitia inhabiting her body, a tonal performance challenge the show builds its identity around. The SBS Drama Awards recognised multiple cast members including Kim Jae-young in supporting honours. The drama averaged 10.8% nationwide ratings - a strong domestic result - and TIME Magazine ranked it sixth on their Best K-Dramas of 2024 list. An 83% Rotten Tomatoes score indicates broadly positive critical reception. Early episodes were noted to accelerate slowly, and the Season 1 finale closes on an open-ended note that set up the already-confirmed Season 2 scheduled for June 2026.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the supernatural premise with committed genre energy: a demon takes human form in a courthouse and immediately begins operating outside the boundaries of Korean law. Park Shin-hye's tonal precision makes the tonal oddity work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Justitia's first act of demonic judgment inside the human legal system - the show announces exactly what it intends to be.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 14
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale resolves most of the episodic villain threads but leaves the central supernatural mission deliberately open - a structural choice that set up the confirmed Season 2.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final confrontation between Justitia and the detective who has pieced together her true identity.
